questions.question: What does @DataJpaTest load?
options: Only JPA entities, repositories and an embedded database
Nothing, it needs a real MySQL server
questions.explanation: @DataJpaTest is a slice test for the data layer and replaces the real database with an embedded one by default.

questions.question: What happens to data saved inside a @DataJpaTest method when the test ends?
options: It stays in the database for the next test
It is rolled back, so the next test starts clean
It is written to a file
questions.explanation: Each test runs in a transaction that is rolled back at the end, which keeps tests independent.

questions.question: A test saves Vanilla 300, Chocolate 450 and Truffle 700 and calls findByPriceLessThan(500). How many cakes come back?
questions.explanation: Vanilla and Chocolate cost less than 500, while Truffle does not, so two rows match.

questions.question: One test saves a book and passes. In the next test, with no @BeforeEach, the code calls books.count(). What does it return?
questions.explanation: The first test was rolled back, so the table is empty at the start of the next test.

questions.question: A @DataJpaTest fails to start because it cannot replace the data source. The pom has the JPA starter and the data JPA test starter only. What is the likely fix?
options: Add an embedded database such as H2 with runtime scope
questions.explanation: The slice swaps in an embedded database, so one such as H2 must be on the classpath.
